# v3.17-dev

## Fixed

**The import summary no longer claims your dates were ambiguous when they plainly weren't.**
Importing an Excel file whose Completed Date column holds real Excel date cells always ended with
this line in the Issues panel:

> All dates fit both DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY — parsed as DD/MM/YYYY (the system default).

It was untrue, and it appeared even for files full of dates like `7/29/2026` that can only be
month-first. **Your dates were always imported correctly** — this was a wrong message, not wrong
data.

The cause: cells that Excel stores as real dates are read by their true underlying value and handed
to the server in an unambiguous form, so the format detector skips them — but it began each check
assuming both formats fitted, and never lowered that assumption when there was nothing to check. A
column with no text dates in it therefore came back as "both formats fit" on the strength of no
evidence at all.

The detector now reports only what it actually read:

- An Excel file whose dates are real date cells says **nothing** about date formats — no ambiguity
  warning, and no "Dates parsed as…" line either, because no format was ever applied to them. One
  fewer entry in the Issues count, too.
- A file that genuinely can't be disambiguated (a CSV of text dates where every day is 1–12) still
  gets the same warning it always did.
- A file that mixes the two now says how many cells the warning is about, e.g. "3 text dates fit
  both DD/MM/YYYY and MM/DD/YYYY", instead of speaking for the whole column.

The "This file looks like MM/DD/YYYY" prompt, the mixed-format rejection, and the day/month-swap
correction are all unchanged.

## Notes

The README and the in-app help now spell out that format detection only ever applied to **text**
date cells, which is what the Native Excel dates section already said.
